title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: OTIS'S PEPPERS
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Otis Greenlee, a shipyard welder from Mobile, Alabama.
Otis can weld a ship in the rain. He cannot boil an egg.
And one spring, his big thumb ordered fifty packets of pepper seeds instead of five.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE PEPPER JUNGLE
segments.quote: Necessity is the mother of invention.
segments.author: Old saying
lines: By July, three hundred pepper plants had eaten his backyard.
His wife Darlene said, Otis, eat them, sell them, or move out with them.
Otis had never cooked a thing. But his grandma had an old saying:
Necessity is the mother of invention.
So Otis bought forty glass bottles and set out to invent a hot sauce.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: TOO HOT
segments.author: Terence
lines: His first batch used every pepper he had, even the scary ones.
His brother-in-law Ray tried one spoon, cried, and drank milk straight from the carton.
Darlene opened every window and quoted Terence, an old Roman playwright:
Moderation in all things.
Otis took out half the peppers and added sweet Alabama peaches. Ray asked for more.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: NOT READY YET
segments.quote: A good plan violently executed now is better than a perfect plan executed next week.
segments.author: George S. Patton
lines: Then Otis tinkered. Version twelve. Version forty-one. Always, it's not ready yet.
His foreman at the shipyard, an old Army man, pointed to a sign from General George Patton:
A good plan violently executed now is better than a perfect plan executed next week.
That night, Otis paid twenty dollars for a table at the Saturday farmers market.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE EMPTY TABLE
segments.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
lines: His first Saturday, Otis sat with his arms crossed, like a bouncer. He sold two bottles. One to Darlene.
Miss Hattie, at the pound cake table, leaned over. Baby, the man who wrote Treasure Island had it right:
Everyone lives by selling something.
So Otis stood up, poured little tastes, and told everyone about the fifty packets. People laughed. Then they bought.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE NEW DISH
segments.quote: The discovery of a new dish does more for the happiness of mankind than the discovery of a star.
segments.author: Jean Anthelme Brillat-Savarin
lines: By August, Miss Hattie dared him to pour his sauce on her pound cake. Otis said, That's crazy.
But her apron had a line from Brillat-Savarin, a French food writer:
The discovery of a new dish does more for the happiness of mankind than the discovery of a star.
Peach pepper pound cake sold out in an hour. A man drove over from Biloxi just to try it.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE RIDE
segments.quote: Your body is not a temple, it's an amusement park. Enjoy the ride.
segments.author: Anthony Bourdain
lines: That fall, Otis printed a real label: Darlene's Fault. Darlene pretended to be mad.
Ray asked if all that spice was smart at fifty-four. Otis grinned and quoted the chef Anthony Bourdain:
Your body is not a temple, it's an amusement park. Enjoy the ride.
Then he ate a whole slice of pound cake, with extra sauce.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Invent. Ease up. Start now. Speak up. Try something new. Enjoy the ride.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Make something of your problem. Ease up. Start now. Speak up. Try something new. And enjoy the ride.
I tried Otis's sauce once. My moustache is still warm.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
